SearchAliases: proper business of a Chan monk
what is the patch-robed monk's proper business
Senses.Note: The exact phrase has 126 hits in 74 works. Six full-case anchors retain direct questions, exclusions of accomplishment, an autobiographical claim, and two different public responses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 獨未是衲僧本分事。於中若得桶底子脫
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu: Yuanwu Keqin bears the exact headword. Yuanwu excludes a catalogue of extraordinary accomplishments from the patch-robed monk’s proper business.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道如何是衲僧本分事？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianyin: Tianyin Yuanxiu bears the exact headword. Tianyin asks directly what the proper business is after excluding spectacular shouts and blows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 未是衲僧本分事。且道如何
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianyin: Tianyin Yuanxiu bears the exact headword. In the preceding clause Tianyin says spectacular shouts and blows are not yet the proper business.

Occurrences.Kwic: 朝參暮請，是我衲僧本分事。然雖如是，要且不是祖師西來意。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan: Poshan Haiming bears the exact headword. Poshan calls travel, talk, and daily attendance the monk’s proper business, then denies that this is the ancestral visitor’s meaning.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是衲僧本分事師便打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L153/L153n1638.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueqiao: Xueqiao Yuanxin bears the exact headword. Xueqiao answers a monk’s direct question by striking him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 作麼生是衲僧本分事。問取堂中二首座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1998A.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui: Dahui Zonggao bears the exact headword. Dahui asks what the proper business is and directs the question to the two appointed seats.

Occurrences.Kwic: 暢衲僧本分之懷。且道是那一句？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe’an: Zhe'an Jingfan bears the exact headword. Zhe’an asks for the one line that opens the proper concern of the patch-robed monk.

Senses.Explanation: A patch-robed monk’s proper business is what remains when accomplishment, verbal display, and borrowed devices are set aside. Masters ask for it directly, deny that spectacular feats amount to it, and answer the question with words or blows that must themselves be met in the interview. Yuanwu Keqin says even extraordinary accomplishments are not yet the patch-robed monk’s proper business, then asks for a statement outside accomplishment. Tianyin Yuanxiu says that even overwhelming shouts and blows are not it, asks what it is, and answers with a verse whose standing peaks do not turn the label into a generic achievement. Poshan Haiming calls ordinary travel and attendance the patch-robed monk’s proper business, but immediately says that this still is not the ancestral visitor’s meaning. Xueqiao Yuanxin answers the direct question with repeated blows. Dahui Zonggao likewise raises the question after listing feats and refers the hearer to the two appointed seats.
